meta.name: Order platform DFMEA, constructed v2 document
meta.scope: The storefront, checkout and fulfilment services and the outside services they reach, constructed to exercise the v2 migration.

included: storefront, checkout and fulfilment and the interfaces they own
excluded: the internals of the hosting platform, its content delivery network and the fraud screening service
boundary.security: No element is security-relevant in this constructed document; a failure whose agent is an adversary would be handed off to threat modeling.

ground_rules: The analysis covers the design of the three in-scope services, not the internals of the services they depend on.

assumptions.text: The payment ledger's 99.95% monthly availability is the platform team's published figure; confirmed by the platform team.

reviews.outcome: The structure and the three chains were reviewed against the platform architecture document and accepted as written.

elements.name: Storefront
elements.description: The shopper-facing web application that browses the catalogue and submits carts.

elements.name: Hosting platform
elements.description: The managed platform that hosts and serves the storefront.

elements.name: Content delivery network
elements.description: The third-party network that caches and delivers the storefront's static assets.

elements.name: Checkout service
elements.description: Turns a submitted cart into a confirmed order once its payment is posted.

elements.name: Payment ledger
elements.description: The append-only store that records each acknowledged payment against its account.

elements.name: Fulfilment service
elements.description: Picks, packs and ships each confirmed order.

elements.name: Fraud screening service
elements.description: A third-party service that scores each order for fraud before it is confirmed.

functions.statement: Post each acknowledged payment to the ledger durably and in order
Confirm an order only after its payment is posted to the ledger

chains.failure_mode: A ledger write is acknowledged and not durably posted

effects.local: The ledger acknowledges a payment it has not stored.
effects.next_level: Checkout treats the payment as posted and confirms the order.
effects.end: An order ships with no ledger record of its payment, and finance must reconstruct it.

causes.text: The ledger acknowledges a write before it is flushed to durable storage

controls.description: Nightly reconciliation of acknowledged ledger writes against stored ledger rows

S.rationale: A missing payment record leaves a shipped order unaccounted for until finance reconstructs it.

O.rationale: The window between acknowledgement and flush is open on every write, and a crash inside it is occasional.

D.rationale: The nightly reconciliation finds every missing row within a day, before the month's books close.

chains.failure_mode: Ledger posts are applied out of order and a balance is computed from a partial sequence

effects.local: The ledger applies a later post before an earlier one for the same account.
effects.next_level: An account balance is computed from a sequence with a gap in it.
effects.end: A shopper or merchant sees a wrong balance until the missing post is applied.

causes.text: Posts for one account are written by concurrent workers with no per-account ordering

controls.description: Sequence-gap alert on ledger posts per account

S.rationale: A wrong balance is visible and corrects itself once the missing post lands, with no money lost.

O.rationale: Concurrent posts to one account are uncommon outside bulk refunds.

D.rationale: The alert fires on a gap only after a grace period, so a short-lived wrong balance can be read first.

chains.failure_mode: Checkout confirms an order whose ledger post failed

effects.local: Checkout reads a failed ledger post as a success.
effects.next_level: The order is confirmed and passed to fulfilment with no posted payment.
effects.end: Goods ship for an order that was never paid for.

causes.text: Checkout treats a ledger timeout as a successful post

controls.description: Daily comparison of confirmed orders against posted ledger entries

S.rationale: Shipping unpaid goods is a direct financial loss that is hard to recover once the order leaves the warehouse.

O.rationale: Ledger timeouts are rare and most of them resolve as successful posts.

D.rationale: The daily comparison names every confirmed order without a ledger entry the next morning.
